reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates TWIP/TRIP activation by interstitial carbon in a metastable fcc/hcp dual-phase HEA, but the hypothesis applies this to a single-phase BCC NbMoTaW system without direct evidence. Key premises about carbon effects in BCC refractory HEAs, avoidance of carbides, and retention of high-temperature strength and irradiation resistance are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Interstitial carbon can activate TWIP/TRIP mechanisms in HEAs
TWIP/TRIP mechanisms improve ductility without sacrificing strength
Low carbon content avoids carbide precipitation that would degrade properties
Interstitial carbon creates local strain fields that promote twinning/phase transformation
The BCC phase and solid-solution strengthening remain intact at high temperature with carbon addition
